No. 
It's been so many years, and this game is still far from finished. And even further from becoming even slightly as fun as the PoP was. Or Persino. Or some other mod for Warband. 
My main gripe is that this game has no challenge in it, like at all. You can try to gimp yourself and make up some dumb masochistic rules, but I really shouldn't be doing that in any game. PoP had giant invasive armies, some of them could even form their own kingdoms by capturing a bunch of settlements. There was always a reason to either be a vassal and strengthen your kingdom, or to make your own. Or you could just take on those armies all by yourself, just to have some fun in beating them alone. 
And what does this game have? Dumb-ass AI that is incapable of... literally anything? Even RBM can't help this game, seriously. 

And some more about the AI; MY GOD it is DUMB. I'm not even sure if you can call it "AI", because they lack any sort of intelligence. On the battlefield, they just build a few formations, and then either press F3, or F1. That's it. And the formations aren't even any different from lord to lord, only different kingdoms have roughly different formations.
Oh, and kingdoms? Absolute clown fiesta. Sometimes lords and even whole armies are just going for a ride in the middle of the enemy territory, and dying like a bunch of lemmings. And sometimes, they just do nothing. 
You will, quite literally, have a single kingdom cornered by 2 or 3 different wars, and they will just sit and do NOTHING. Their opponents may even be in an alliance, and yet, they'll just AFK in their towns, waiting for the harvesting season. 

The economy in this game is in even worse state. Like, you just do an early-game money making method, and then you fight a bunch, and now you have an infinite flow of money. Woah. 

Your PC is also completely unimportant, unlike how it was in PoP. You might as well remove your character from the game, HELL, you CAN JUST GO AND BECOME A HERMIT, AND MAKE YOUR LVL30 TERMINATOR WIFE A KING.
Like, what is the point of your existence even? Especially on the battlefield. 

And quests? They've added stealth mechanics and shit,, but WHY? You don't need those quests. They don't give you ANYTHING of worth. ABSOLUTELY NOTHING. Releplay purposes? Well, I can go and replay KCD1/2 if I want some medieval roleplay. 

And this is not like they are improving the game. It's getting WORSE, not better. Man, you probably don't even want to buy their DLC, just because it feels more like a very underbaked and unnecessary mod rather than an official DLC. Also, DLC in an early access game. Classic. 

TL:DR - Just play PoP for Warband, not this pointlessly grindy (and just generally pointless) piece of early access. 
Maybe sometime later down the line, taleworlds finally will open their eyes and do to this game whatever IndieStone have done to PZ. Maybe...

Had the review thumbnail appear in my profile for absolutely ages now and always put it off because I don't really know what to say to adequately describe truly how good this masterpiece is. I've not played it in a few weeks now so I have the benefit of not wanting to play it again (temporarily), because I'd normally just click the play button.
Ironically, by not actually  playing the game for a few weeks it has made me appreciate even more how spectacular this game really iss.

To all people that have never played any Mount and Blade game before:

It's really quite tricky to describe the sort of game this is because it really is it's own genre in a way (or should be).
I'll try my best, so here it goes -
It is a fully sandbox fantasy medieval RPG (and I mean FULLY - the campaign mode is basically the same as the sandbox mode but it essentially just gives you tutorials and starting family members, which are really useful to have in your first play through). 
If you like big budget story driven top graphic RPG's, this definitely is not for you. It is none of those things.
It has literally no story line - because YOU make the story.
It isn't big budget - it's taleworlds.
It's got fantastic battle graphics despite it's low budget, but it's not on the scale of all the big boys.

What really makes this game is the literally infinite possibilities.
You can literally do anything.

Everybody starts off with a set of clothes and a horse. (If you do campaign mode you also start off with a brother and sisters, which help massively building your clan).
The rest is up to you.
If you want to become a bandit - and build a group of bandits that raid and pillage towns/villages - you can.
If you want to be a trader, mind your own business, not hurt anybody, and just trade goods / buy and run your own workshops - you can.
If you want to become a leader of your own band of warriors and get factions to pay you as a mercenary to fight for them - you can.
If you want to be a great fighter and just wander from town to town fighting in arenas to gain renown - you can.
If you want to prove yourself in battle and join a faction as a vassal, to fight for your king/liege and prove your worth and get rich - you can.
If you'd rather create your own faction and gain your own lands , and eventually rule the whole world - you can.
It has absolutely everything.
If you'd rather not war or trade, but want to spend your time in the smithy, breaking down raw materials and/or crafting weapons for a profit or for favour with NPC's - you can!
In any of these potential avenues, you can marry and have children - or not. It's completely up to you.
The game environment is different every time you play it. The  world economy runs as its own unique economy each playthrough. What might work one playthrough, might not  necessarily work in another..Or it might?.

Having said everything I have said, the game DOES revolve mostly around fighting. You WILL need to be somewhat competent as a fighter (although I know of people who have done completely pacifist saves without fighting at all as traders - but it is  difficult).
With this in mind, the battle/combat system is basically like playing a Total War game (any of them), except you are issuing instructions to your troops whilst being physically present as a character on the battlefield.
Want to focus more on the strategy, rather than fight? You can.
Want to  dart about on your horse (or dismount and go on foot?) with a massive axe or crossbow ((or  normal bow, 2h sword, or  1h + shield, or mace (1h or 2h), or polearm or bare knuckles)),  smashing people in battle and leave the strategy to your sergeants? You can.
Want to do a bit of both? You can.
Then comes the absolute best bit of the battles which i didn't even mention yet - sieges.
Build trebuchets, onagers, balistas, siege towers, battering rams. Operate them yourself in the siege. Climb up the ladders yourself. Command which units go up ladders, which go in towers, which go where. On the battlefield like total war, except you're actually fighting it like in an RPG.
Defending against a siege? You can do the same. You can even pick up the siege ammunition without a siege weapon and throw them through the castle/settlement walls at the enemy!
You can auto resolve all battles as well like in TW, if you don't want to fight a particular battle or siege.

There's honestly 100 other things I can't cram in to this right now, but the main thing is there are some absolutely unbelievable mods that have been designed by the community that expand and improve QoL, but also mods that change the game entirely. All for free.

Honestly, Bannerlord feels almost exactly like Mount & Blade: Warband, just with better graphics and a more modern presentation. The core gameplay, combat, and overall gameplay loop feel remarkably similar, and after playing it, I struggle to understand what makes this worth such a high price. I expected a sequel to bring more meaningful improvements and a genuinely different experience, but instead, it feels like I’m paying a premium to play essentially the same game I played years ago. The combat doesn’t feel particularly revolutionary, and much of the gameplay feels like a repeat of Warband with a fresh coat of paint.
I understand that there are improvements to graphics, battles, and certain systems, but personally, they aren’t enough to justify the price. For a game this expensive, I expected more substantial changes to the core experience.

If you already own Warband, I’d have a hard time recommending Bannerlord at full price unless you’re specifically looking for better graphics and larger-scale battles. For me, the overall experience just doesn’t feel different enough to justify the cost.

TLDR: I would have loved to see extra time and care put into this game, as I feel the core gameplay loop is great.

I feel devastated when I play this game because of the wasted potential that I am reminded of. The core loop of building  your army, sieging enemy fortresses and fighting battle after battle is incredibly addicting. However, I feel like the game is missing the more in depth aspects that would make it a masterpiece and a genre defining title. Certain parts of the game lack depth and can be frustrating to engage with. Diplomacy, dialogue, familial systems, companion systems, and battlefield strategy feel like aspects of the game that weren't given enough love by the devs, which is frustrating because in the late game they are tend to be important systems that need can't be ignored. 

I have to commend the devs on building a world that doesn't make you the main character. I absolutely love the feeling that everyone has independent motivations, and seeing all the armies and caravans go about their business is great. However, it's an illusion that quickly falls away once you gain more power in your playthrough. Ultimately the goal of becoming the ruler of the lands makes for a fun, engaging game with a strong core loop. I just feel sad when I think about how much more interesting the game could be if it had more depth.

Mount & Blade II: Bannerlord is a good game overall and one of the most interesting medieval sandbox games available. Building your clan, creating your own kingdom, commanding armies, and fighting massive battles can keep you entertained for hundreds of hours. The game offers a level of freedom that very few strategy RPGs can match.

My biggest issue with the game is the lack of a co-op campaign. Bannerlord feels like the perfect game to play with friends. Imagine leading different clans in the same world, fighting together in battles, managing kingdoms, or conquering Calradia as a team. It is disappointing that this feature was never added, and I honestly believe it is the game's biggest weakness. I hope that if Bannerlord 3 ever gets made, TaleWorlds finally adds a proper co-op mode.

Another major problem is smithing. The system is extremely unbalanced. You can start with around 5,000 coins and, after only 2-3 hours of smithing, end up with several million. This makes trading, workshops, caravans, and many other money-making methods feel almost pointless.

The problem is that you cannot simply ignore smithing either. While you can choose not to use it for making money, you will miss out on some of the best weapons in the game. Crafted weapons can easily outperform most equipment you can find or buy, making smithing feel almost mandatory if you want the strongest gear.

I also think the crafting system could be expanded. It would be great if we could craft armor, not stronger or unique armor, but simply the armor pieces that already exist in the game. Sometimes finding a specific armor set is a complete headache because of how random shops and loot can be. Being able to craft existing armor for yourself and your troops would be a great quality-of-life feature without hurting game balance.

Another feature I would love to see is the ability to create custom troop trees. Instead of relying entirely on existing faction troops, players could design and equip their own units. Creating a unique army that reflects your kingdom's culture and fighting style would make the late game much more enjoyable and add another layer of customization.

Combat is generally good, but some mechanics feel questionable. Crossbows not being able to penetrate shields feels strange. It is also a bit silly when a fully maxed-out warrior with a two-handed sword or axe gets his attack blocked by an enemy carrying a tiny wooden hammer. These moments can break immersion and make combat feel less believable than it should.

The AI is decent, but nothing special. It is not terrible, but it is far from great. Sometimes kingdoms gather huge armies only to run around the map without accomplishing much. Instead of capturing settlements or defending their territory, they often wander around seemingly without a clear objective.

One mechanic that I actually like is that axes and some polearms can cleave through multiple enemies in a single swing. It makes weapon choice more meaningful and gives those weapons a unique advantage. At the same time, it is disappointing that most other weapons cannot do the same. A massive two-handed greatsword should not stop after hitting a single enemy while an axe can cut through several soldiers. I think more weapon types should have access to this mechanic, especially larger two-handed weapons.

Another thing that stands out is how much the game relies on its modding community. Sometimes it feels like Bannerlord is still alive because of modders constantly adding new content, fixing issues, and expanding gameplay. It is great that the community is so passionate and talented, and many mods genuinely improve the game. However, I think the developers should be doing more themselves instead of relying on the community to solve many of the game's shortcomings.

A good example is the Diplomacy mod. Features from that mod should already be part of the base game. Managing a kingdom can become frustrating because you often have to chase NPCs all over the map just to talk to them. For example, recruiting a clan to your kingdom can turn into a long game of hide-and-seek. Diplomatic actions should be easier to handle, and some form of messaging system, diplomacy menu, or improved kingdom management would make the experience much smoother.

As for multiplayer, it is mostly for a specific audience. Some players enjoy it a lot, while others will spend almost all their time in single-player. It is not bad, but it feels less popular and less interesting than the campaign experience.

Overall, Mount & Blade II: Bannerlord is a very good game with excellent large-scale battles, a unique sandbox experience, and plenty of replayability. Despite issues such as unbalanced smithing, average AI, basic diplomacy, and some questionable combat mechanics, the game remains one of the best medieval war simulators available today. However, the missing co-op campaign is what prevents it from reaching its full potential for me.

I hope TaleWorlds learns from Bannerlord's strengths and weaknesses and makes Bannerlord 3 a much better game. If they add co-op, improve diplomacy, balance smithing, introduce custom troop creation, armor crafting, smarter AI, and larger battles, I genuinely believe it could dominate the medieval sandbox genre for a very long time.

I'm also looking forward to Chronicles: Medieval, which is currently planned for release in 2027. Competition is always good because it pushes developers to improve their games. I think Chronicles: Medieval has the potential to be a strong competitor to Bannerlord 2. However, if TaleWorlds addresses the major issues mentioned above in a future Bannerlord 3, I believe it would be on another level entirely and could remain the dominant medieval warfare sandbox game for years.

There is a Mod that seems like it would fit into Bannerlord perfectly, I beg of you, make the "DynaCulture" mod a vanilla Sandbox modifier, Please. A quick rundown on what it does, if a faction holds a fief for long enough, that fief will start changing cultures, there's a lot of options for it, but even a basic version would be loved. A note that I really like, the culture change is NOT instant, recruits from villages will be half and half, I also pair it with the "Change a Vassals Culture" and "Change a Companions Culture". Seeing this introduced would be one of the coolest things ever, and with the recent additions to the sandbox mode, it seems more possible than ever. Imagine being in the Nordic faction, and sailing all the way around the world to conquer the Aserai, just to make a "Southern Nordic Enclave. This could really introduce new goals for the game, not to conquer, but to make a kingdom of enclaves all over and try to protect them. Watching kingdoms change borders, and having their culture follow could be the coolest thing ever, not to mention it would make it easier for players to create custom maps.
I LOVE the game, and don't want to have this come up as useless criticism, but I truly beg of you to let vanilla-only player experience that side of bannerlord.
